The current evidence does not establish a cycle phase or distribution: positive recent returns, positive proxy breadth and short-window aggressive flows coexist with negative 69-hour returns, weak rotation readings and persistent ETH/BTC weakness.

Legacy pullback hypotheses partially match the current relative-weakness and medium-window price evidence, but the breadth and flow sequence is mixed; this is not sufficient to treat the legacy hypothesis as confirmed.

The nominal 12-, 24- and 72-hour windows span 9, 21 and 69 hours, respectively; interpret them by actual span, not as full nominal windows.
ETH/BTC persistence is based on the supplied 168 hourly direct closes; it does not by itself establish broad altcoin-market participation or a cycle phase.
Breadth is a point-in-time top-100 proxy with changing membership and is explicitly unconfirmed as canonical broad-alt or large-cap breadth.
ETF evidence here is one settled session; missing sessions are not imputed. Current stablecoin supply data is supply-liquidity context, not confirmation of deployed demand.
Liquidation data has unverified completeness and rolling-window limitations. Option moneyness skew is not 25-delta skew and lacks an equivalent historical snapshot.
News coverage has a degraded owner state and one unverified item despite PASS coverage status; verified context is empty, so event coverage remains uncertain.
